Consider [MATH: \triangle ABC] shown above. The line segment [MATH: \overline{CH}] is the altitude corresponding to [MATH: \overline{AB}.] If [MATH: m\angle BAC = 115^\circ,] calculate [MATH: m\angle HCA.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Since the straight angle must have a measure of [MATH: 180^\circ,] we have [MATH: m∠HAC + m∠BAC|= 180^{∘}; m∠HAC + 115^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; m∠HAC|= 65^{∘}.]

Note that [MATH: \triangle ACH] is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to [MATH: 180^\circ,] we have [MATH: m∠HCA + m∠HAC + m∠AHC|= 180^{∘}; m∠HCA + 65^{∘} + 90^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; m∠HCA + 155^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; m∠HCA|= 25^{∘}.]
